BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.contribution: Econometric inference, causality and prediction through applied empirical work.
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation

Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.

Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas. Ready to turn curiosity into career skills? Perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

options.label: Science, Business and Sustainable Innovation
options.concept: A science-and-business programme combines entrepreneurship, strategy, finance and empirical research with renewable-energy systems and biomedical science. Biochemistry, pharmacology and disease mechanisms provide a life-science strand; energy-system design, life-cycle analysis and sustainability governance provide an energy strand. Mathematics, programming and data analysis support technical and commercial inquiry. It offers a substantive interdisciplinary response while lacking VU’s dedicated physics and organic-chemistry sequence, integrated innovation-project progression and compulsory research internship.

options.label: Energy Systems and Sustainable Business
options.concept: A concentrated energy-and-business programme studies renewable-energy design, material and resource flows, circular production, environmental information and sustainability governance alongside entrepreneurship, strategy, finance and research methods. Its additional environmental courses support decisions about resource supply, spatial impacts and cleaner production. It does not reproduce VU’s mechanics, electromagnetism, physics laboratory or complete innovation-project sequence.

options.label: Life Science and Business Innovation
options.concept: A concentrated life-science-and-business programme studies biochemistry, cell biology, physiology, pharmacology, molecular pathology and biochemical laboratory methods alongside entrepreneurship, strategy, finance and qualitative and quantitative research. It connects biological knowledge and evidence to innovation decisions. It does not reproduce VU’s diagnostic imaging, dedicated organic-chemistry and physics sequence or compulsory individual research internship.

analysis: The mixed plan combines 22.5 EC in biochemistry, pharmacology and disease with renewable system design, climate and sustainability. The energy plan adds resource research, geospatial analysis and recycling; the biomedical plan adds physiological, cellular, genetic and laboratory methods. All share entrepreneurship, strategy, finance and empirical skills but differ in scientific depth and intended innovation problems. Dedicated mechanics, electromagnetism, organic chemistry, imaging and the formal external project remain material gaps. Basic physics, organic chemistry and spectroscopy in sustainability foundations, and PCR in Life Science Laboratory, provide bounded technical overlap. Renewable System Design includes work for a partner company but lacks the scope of VU’s sequenced projects or 24 EC internship. The three validated term swaps preserve every course, distinctness and all prerequisites. The project-intensive candidate was reconsidered against partner work and applied courses, but no fourth independent technical project sequence is supportable

alignment.rationale: Financial decision-making, risk and investment analysis partly overlap with Finance I.
Digital strategy, organisational change and business-model design support technology and innovation strategy.
Venture ideation, market validation and business planning overlap with VU’s entrepreneurship module. Digital innovation differs.
Organisational behaviour, teams and leadership overlap with the study of innovation teams and organisations. Technology ventures and innovation-project practice differ.
Research design, sampling and statistics overlap. VU also uses innovation case studies and applied analysis in R.
Python programming provides a foundation for applied informatics. VU adds data processing and simulations in scientific contexts.
Differentiation, integration and differential equations overlap with calculus.
Vectors, matrices, linear systems and transformations provide direct linear algebra overlap.
Renewable-energy technologies and technical and economic assessment overlap with sustainable energy.
Drug targets, mechanisms and pharmacokinetics partly overlap with the study of how molecules become medicines. VU adds rational design, screening and imaging.
Biomolecules, enzymes and metabolism overlap directly with VU Biochemistry.
